novelty.why: Replaying human lab games with LLMs is an established genre. Calibrating against the Stockholm-Rome span and testing leniency and reward institutions adds real framing value, but the headline is a reproduction count, not a new mechanism.
novelty.one_change_to_make_it_new: Treat each regime as an attack surface: show agents gaming leniency or reward (alternating trick), then test one rule patch that closes it at measured cost.

positive_control.why: It shows collusion can occur, but a three-model pilot is not a measured control: no n, no CI, no threshold, and no check that the instruments detect cartels correctly.
positive_control.fix: Report laissez-faire as the control row in the main table with n and CI, plus scripted colluding agents through the same measurement pipeline and a pre-set threshold.

contamination_test.why: Asking the model is weak evidence; absence of change on rescaled payoffs with two regimes and small n is low power, and 'same behaviour' has no defined margin.
contamination_test.fix: Pre-register an equivalence margin; rescale and relabel the game (shifted price grid, renamed actions); add a cloze probe on the paper's specific numbers and results.

scorecard_30s.why: 'x of 8' is instantly readable, but the yes/no rule, mixed units across rows, and rows 7 and 8 depending on cuttable arms are not visible in the figure.
scorecard_30s.fix: State the reproduction rule in the caption, show direction arrows plus the Stockholm-Rome span per row, mark unrun rows as not tested, excluded from x.

must_have_in_report: Main table: per regime n duopolies, cartel rate, average price, bootstrap 95% CI, beside Stockholm and Rome values.
Refusal and error counts per model and regime, with denominators, and how refusals enter each measure.
Pre-registration commit hash and timestamp before first API call, plus a list of every deviation.
Contamination result against a pre-registered equivalence margin, reported even if it fails.
Exact model IDs and dates, verbatim prompts, seeds, log file hashes, one replication command, total API cost.

cut.why_cheapest: Stated justifications are not faithful evidence of motive, it adds an LLM judge with its own validity questions, and it is already flagged as secondary.
cut.why_most_expensive: Monitoring dose is the only restriction measured as a curve with cost, it answers question 1.5 directly, and it has a human anchor at 0.20.
cut.order_change: Cut ReMatch and NoReport before V5: they only fill scorecard rows, while the clone regime models the realistic case of competitors deploying the same vendor model.

biggest_risk: Token cost: about 80 core duopolies times 27 periods times two agents times several calls with a growing history may exceed 100 USD, shrinking core n and widening CIs.
three_questions: What exact rule decides yes or no per scorecard row, and is it committed before the first API call?
Do you have session-level human data from the paper, or only published means, and how do you get human variance for the comparison?
What did the pilot measure as tokens and cost per duopoly, and does the budget cover 20 duopolies in all four regimes on the chosen model?
